- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (especially sentiment > 0.8) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low or negative (sentiment < 0.27) — model shows mean-reversion bias, underreacting to downward pressure.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model often reacts 1–2 days after sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns positive.
- Overweight recent price momentum in forecasts — model ignores 3–5 day mean reversion, leading to persistent over/underestimation.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model fails to adjust forecast horizon — tends to smooth out extremes, missing sharp reversals.
- Forecast bias toward higher prices in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is bullish — model overconfident in short-term momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model defaults to historical mean — fails to capture sentiment-driven deviations from trend.
